name: XOŞKÎN
description: Xoşkîn is a Kurdish trick-taking card game similar to 3-player double-deck Pinochle. Played in eastern/southeastern Turkey (Northern Kurdistan). Features bidding and melds. Also known as Nezere or Pinîkêr. Name possibly derived from English 'Auction' via 'Okşin'.

content.text: Xoşkîn is a Kurdish trick-taking card game similar to 3-player double-deck Pinochle. Played in eastern/southeastern Turkey (Northern Kurdistan). Features bidding and melds. Also known as Nezere or Pinîkêr. Name possibly derived from English 'Auction' via 'Okşin'.

This Kurdish trick-taking game with bidding is played in the eastern and south-eastern parts of Turkey, unofficially known as northern Kurdistan. Xoşkîn is almost identical to the American game of three-handed double deck Pinochle; the alternative name Pinîkêr reflects that. As Levent Suberk suggested, the name Xoşkîn likely derives from the English 'Auction', probably via 'Okşin'. A version played by Turkish workers in Düsseldorf has been documented by Thomas Beil.
Cards dealt to 3 players with widow.
